head: 652b8115080e5e97b2274cb602de3faf8c551f20
target: For every independent sequence of stopped standard Brownian pieces indexed by all integers, with stopping times 0<=T_k<c a.s. for one deterministic finite c and divergent sums in both directions, does the continuous concatenation admit one a.s. finite real random S at which its centered forward and centered time-reversed halves are independent standard Brownian motions?
probability_quantifiers: A property of the given concatenation law. S may depend on the full path and extra randomness; no stopping-time property of S is stated. Exact joint law of both complete halves is required.
concatenation: S_0=0; S_{k+1}-S_k=T_k; X_0=0; X_{S_k+t}-X_{S_k}=B^k_t for 0<=t<T_k, extended continuously at joins. Negative pieces retain increasing-time orientation; observing X_{-t} reverses each path and reverses the indexed concatenation order.
assumptions: Joint stopped pieces (T_k,B^k_[0,T_k]) are independent. They need not be identically distributed.
Each B^k is standard Brownian motion for its specified stopping-time filtration. Any filtration enlargement must retain the Brownian property; anticipation is excluded.
All T_k>=0 are a.s. finite. Zero lengths are permitted and removed harmlessly; the divergent sums exclude a finite-time accumulation of infinitely many indexed positive lengths.
One deterministic strict common bound T_k<c a.s. applies to every k. A pathwise bound depending on omega, per-index bounds growing with k, or uniform finite moments are different assumptions.
The source definition of two-sided Brownian motion is random-origin existence. At the distinguished join 0 the negative half need not be Brownian.
success_criteria: A checkable proof yielding one finite random shift S with both halves having the exact independent Wiener joint law, or an admissible bounded counterexample excluding every possible such S.
For partial claims, verify only their stated output; pathwise approximation, rescaling limits, stationary/equilibrium replacements, and randomized rotations do not alone prove the source target.
boundary_cases: T_k=0 for arbitrary indices; non-iid positive durations; nonintegrable index count in bounded intervals; c=0 gives no admissible divergent construction.
Stopping-time dependence of (T,B_T), bias after time reversal, negative-side ordering and filtration.
Random-origin shift could be non-stopping; independence of the two halves cannot be inferred from a marginal Gaussian limit.
pre_partial_independent_mechanism: Forward gluing from a fixed indexed join follows strong Markov concatenation. Bounded optional sampling controls terminal moments but does not make reversed stopped paths Brownian. Any claim that rotation at a stopping time preserves a deterministic Brownian block law must be proved, including dependence of chosen rotation on the block. An iid equilibrium/Palm origin would alter the general non-iid source model and cannot be silently substituted.
